criteria.criterion: IDs start at 1 and increase by one per added item. An ID is never reused, even after its item
criteria.reason: `_next_id` starts at 1, increments on each add, and is saved to the file. Deleting an item does not decrement it, so IDs are not reused, including across reloads.

criteria.criterion: `complete` and `delete` raise `KeyError` for an ID that does not exist. Completing an item that

criteria.criterion: `items()` returns copies, so changing the returned dicts does not change the stored list.
criteria.reason: `items()` returns `dict(i)` copies. The item values are flat (int, str, bool), so a shallow copy is enough.

criteria.criterion: Every change is saved to the file right away. A second `TodoList(path)` sees all earlier
criteria.reason: `add`, `complete` and `delete` each call `_save()`, which writes atomically with a temp file and `os.replace`. `__init__` loads items and `next_id` from the file.

criteria.criterion: Only the Python standard library is used.
